canonical_statement: Mortality implies a propensity for error or sin.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou art but mortal. If thou hast sinned, do so no more.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can perceive and interact with another consciousness across vast distances without physical proximity.

attributions.surface_quote: In Umaur I can see thee, and bear thee, and love thee, dear, for I shall not this time remove the naim, so that it will be much as if I were here.

canonical_statement: A specific technology or method exists that allows for the extraction of water from the atmosphere.

attributions.surface_quote: the electric generator of water... result was rapid deposition of moisture from the atmosphere.

canonical_statement: The physical structures of ancient civilizations can endure for vast periods, defying typical rates of decay.

attributions.surface_quote: even a stone structure should so long have withstood the effects of time

canonical_statement: The existence of ancient civilizations can be entirely forgotten, even by other long-lived civilizations.

attributions.surface_quote: relic of some people so ancient as to antedate even Poseid's forty centuries

canonical_statement: The divine entity, referred to by various names, attends to the needs of its creations, but its judgment of what constitutes a primary need may differ from the perception of the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: God, Incal, Brahm, call the Eternal Spirit what thou wilt--verily doth heed the needs of His children, but those needs which to the child seem to be uppermost, are not always so adjudged by the Eternal One.

canonical_statement: The divine entity operates through its creations, fostering interdependence among them, such that assistance often manifests through other beings.

attributions.surface_quote: He operates through His children, whether human or angelic ones, making each one interdependent with all others, and thus men or angels may have for helpers each other, or perhaps only some animal brother.

canonical_statement: Divine intervention or aid often occurs indirectly, mediated by the actions or emotions of other beings, such as self-interest or pity.

attributions.surface_quote: God noteth a drowning mariner, but unless some brother be there to rescue, he may physically perish. He tempereth the wind to the shorn lamb, but generally only through the fact that self interest, or it may be some higher emotion, as pity, is aroused in the mind of beholding man.

canonical_statement: The physical body, mind, and spirit each have distinct modes of prayer and receive answers specific to their nature.

attributions.surface_quote: the physical body must pray with muscular action...the mind must pray through mental processes...the Spirit shall pray through its spiritual nature

canonical_statement: Effective prayer requires alignment between the physical, mental, and spiritual aspects of an individual.

attributions.surface_quote: if the mind pray not also, knowledge will not come to the brain. How shall the mind pray? By being in harmony with the Spirit.

canonical_statement: Mental influence or clairvoyance can be obstructed by external forces or entities.

attributions.surface_quote: the enemy who had aroused my curiosity to work my ruin intercepted all such clairvoyant messages

canonical_statement: Conscious beings can project their consciousness or 'subtle body' to distant locations, leaving their physical form in a trance.

attributions.surface_quote: he possessed the power to lay aside the gross body of earth as one would an overcoat and project himself to any desired place.

canonical_statement: A higher power can communicate knowledge of an individual's predicament to another being.

attributions.surface_quote: he had become aware of my unpleasant predicament through Incal

canonical_statement: The concept of 'God' as a singular, divine entity is a human construct, an empty ideal born of fancy, rather than an objective reality.

attributions.surface_quote: God! There is no God. Bah! how blind men are to pray to such empty ideals as their fancies name 'God!'

canonical_statement: Different cultures attribute the title 'God' to various figures, demonstrating the subjective and culturally relative nature of divine concepts.

attributions.surface_quote: Men of Poseid say Incal is God; men of Suernis say Yeovah, and they of Necropan say Osiris.

canonical_statement: Entities can exist across multiple incarnations or lifetimes.

attributions.surface_quote: I came from a former life on earth, aye! many of them

canonical_statement: The future is predetermined and recorded in a 'Book of Fate'.

attributions.surface_quote: in the Book of Fate I do not find it so written

canonical_statement: Some beings possess the ability to perceive or 'read' the predetermined future.

attributions.surface_quote: I have lost my power to read fate

canonical_statement: Individuals can retain identity and grievances across multiple incarnations.

attributions.surface_quote: I follow her in vengeance. To wring her soul in agony

canonical_statement: Some beings possess vast power to foresee and manipulate future events.

attributions.surface_quote: being gifted with vast power of forpiercing the future

canonical_statement: There exists a secret or method to prolong life indefinitely.

attributions.surface_quote: I have long known a secret which prolongs life

canonical_statement: The physical body can be sustained for an extended duration beyond common human experience through esoteric means.

attributions.surface_quote: I have worked for three centuries in this present body.

canonical_statement: There exist non-human, evil entities that can be mastered and utilized.

attributions.surface_quote: obtained mastery over the evil hosts which are not human, never were, and never will be.

canonical_statement: Conflict between forces of 'light' and 'dark' operates by influencing the 'animal nature' of humanity.

attributions.surface_quote: both work on the animal nature of man, which, having no light of guidance, taketh the first offered support

canonical_statement: Divine beings can manifest physically in response to challenges.

attributions.surface_quote: A human form, which yet was not of earth, surrounded by a blinding white light, stood before us. Was this Incal?

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess a countenance that transcends human emotion.

attributions.surface_quote: Upon His countenance rested a calm but awful expression, though not of anger or any human emotion.

canonical_statement: All individuals possess self-mastery over their actions and choices.

attributions.surface_quote: thou art thine own master, even as all men are self-masters

canonical_statement: An individual's wisdom, when misapplied to selfish or destructive ends, leads to their downfall.

attributions.surface_quote: thine altitude of wisdom, prostituted to selfishness... is thy destruction

canonical_statement: An 'ego' is an eternal, indestructible emanation from a higher divine source.

attributions.surface_quote: as thou art an ego, a ray from my Father... this may not be of an ego

canonical_statement: An 'ego' cannot cease to exist, even if its actions warrant such a fate.

attributions.surface_quote: It were better for thee couldst thou cease to exist. But this may not be of an ego.

canonical_statement: A human entity can be suspended and transformed into a power of nature as a form of divine judgment.

attributions.surface_quote: I can but suspend thee as a human entity and cast thee into the outer darkness to serve as one of the powers of nature.

canonical_statement: The ultimate judge of individuals is an infinite, divine being, referred to as Christ.

attributions.surface_quote: the Judge was Man, and more than Man finite--was MAN INFINITE, even CHRIST.

canonical_statement: The physical body is not the essential self, but a temporary vessel for physical life.

attributions.surface_quote: the earthly frame is no more an essential of the real man than the cocoon is a part of the butterfly

canonical_statement: An individual can achieve a state of perfection, embodying a divine principle while remaining human.

attributions.surface_quote: I am reached unto the perfection of the Seventh Principle and am Man, also the Son of Man

canonical_statement: All individuals are fundamentally connected as children of a singular divine source.

attributions.surface_quote: are we not all children of One, our Father?

canonical_statement: The divine spirit present in one perfected being is also the inherent spirit of every human.

attributions.surface_quote: That which I am, the Spirit of every man is.

canonical_statement: Annihilation of existence is impossible.

attributions.surface_quote: annihilation, which can not be

canonical_statement: Death can be a transition, but also a state of living no longer as human life, exiled to a state of 'devildom'.

attributions.surface_quote: death which is transition, but the death which liveth no more as human life

canonical_statement: The soul can exist independently of the physical body and is not harmed by the body's destruction.

attributions.surface_quote: I, that am become Jesus the Christ, not be harmed, but mine earthly house only.

canonical_statement: Reincarnation is a process by which souls return to Earth in new physical forms.

attributions.surface_quote: until she hath gone from Earth twice and come again, and shall be called Phyris.

canonical_statement: A soul can incarnate as a 'perfect human soul' to achieve a specific spiritual purpose, such as overcoming death.

attributions.surface_quote: I will enter in and dwell as a perfect human soul, and make that Man first fruit of them that sleep the sleep which is change, so that by me he shall be exalted above Death.

canonical_statement: The physical world and all existence are ultimately manifestations or possessions of a divine entity.

attributions.surface_quote: I speak great words of GOD,--and the world is His.

canonical_statement: The state of being 'dead' involves the separation of consciousness from the physical body, which is left behind as a 'shell'.

attributions.surface_quote: behind me, as a shell, remained the poor clay casket

canonical_statement: The experience of death can initially feel natural and similar to vivid dreams, or even earth-life, rather than a radical departure.

attributions.surface_quote: All was as natural in seeming as are things in vivid dreams. ... differed not at all from earth-life

canonical_statement: After death, individual identities may transform, such that former relationships are not maintained in their original form.

attributions.surface_quote: not then as Anzimee, nor would I then be Zailm

canonical_statement: Spiritual understanding may be limited by the 'natural mind', which struggles to grasp 'spiritual meaning'.

attributions.surface_quote: my natural mind was not able to grasp its spiritual meaning

canonical_statement: There are different stages or layers of the afterlife, and a further process ('Maxin-Light') may be required to reach a 'real' or deeper state.

attributions.surface_quote: pass through the Maxin-Light. ... finding the real Navazzamin

canonical_statement: The process of purging 'earthiness' is necessary to access a more profound spiritual reality in the afterlife.

attributions.surface_quote: purge away the earthiness which possibly prevented my finding the real Navazzamin

canonical_statement: Consciousness can exist independently of a physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: being dead I could not need such transportation

canonical_statement: Non-physical entities can influence the physical world.

attributions.surface_quote: The farther I got the more uneasy he became... he started after me

canonical_statement: Animals can perceive non-physical presences, even if humans cannot.

attributions.surface_quote: He was awake to a sense of my presence, though he could not see, feel or hear me.

canonical_statement: Physical sensations like fatigue, hunger, and thirst are tied to the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: feeling no fatigue, nor hunger nor thirst, nor any sensation of the physical life

canonical_statement: Non-physical entities can directly influence human actions, even to the point of mechanical compliance.

attributions.surface_quote: I said to the man: 'Use that pen.' ... he use it, but seemed in a deep sleep

canonical_statement: A discarnate consciousness can temporarily control a living body and use it for communication.

attributions.surface_quote: for the time I was the controlling intelligence of his body.

canonical_statement: A discarnate consciousness can instantaneously transport itself to a desired location through intent.

attributions.surface_quote: With this utterance all things changed, and I found myself in the palace of Agacoe.

canonical_statement: Death is a barrier between two conditions of existence, making communication between the living and the dead difficult or impossible.

attributions.surface_quote: Was death indeed the threshold between two conditions, communication to and fro being impossible...?

canonical_statement: Some individuals can temporarily leave their physical bodies to travel and then return to them at will.

attributions.surface_quote: he could see those who put off their fleshly shells in order to travel as Mainin had done, and resume them at will

canonical_statement: Death may involve a more profound separation than merely shedding the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: Death perhaps meant more even than putting aside the body.

canonical_statement: The process of dying involves the separation of an individual into three distinct psychic elements: an earthly component, a psychic component, and a spiritual component.
The highest aspect of an individual's being is the 'I Am' or ego.
After death, a 'shell' or earthly component remains in earthly conditions until the physical body fully dissolves.
The ego, or 'I Am', seeks an exalted level of existence after death.
An individual can exist in multiple forms or counterparts simultaneously, including a material image, an intermediate counterpart, and an invisible self.
The egoic state is characterized by isolation.

attributions.surface_quote: The exalted or egoic state is one of isolation.

canonical_statement: After death, the ego cannot return to the earthly plane or perceive earthly matters, except through intense mental-spiritual states of living individuals.

attributions.surface_quote: the ego, after a little while, cannot return to earth, nor know anything earthly save those extremely tense mental-spiritual states

canonical_statement: Genuine mediumship involves the medium ascending to a higher spiritual state, rather than the departed ego descending to the earthly plane.

attributions.surface_quote: The genuine medium rises to the necessary height, but the ego can not descend to earth

canonical_statement: The law of progress dictates that the ego cannot retrogress, except for a limited period after death, which is not true retrogression.

attributions.surface_quote: the ego can not descend to earth, can not deny the law of progress, except during a limited period after the transition called death

canonical_statement: The departed do not return to the earthly plane except through physical rebirth and reincarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: There is no return of the departed, except through physical rebirth and reincarnation.

canonical_statement: Transmigration of souls, which postulates rebirth in lower animal forms as punishment, is a false concept.

attributions.surface_quote: this is not transmigration of souls, for the latter postulates rebirth in lower animal form as a punishment for sin; such a thing can not be.

canonical_statement: Retrogression of the soul is impossible.

attributions.surface_quote: Retrogression is impossible

canonical_statement: Successive rebirths in reincarnation are invariably progressive.

attributions.surface_quote: reincarnation, whose successive rebirths are invariably progressive.

canonical_statement: All beings are children of one Father, implying a fundamental spiritual equality.

attributions.surface_quote: Ye are all Children of one Father!

canonical_statement: An ego is prevented by its fundamental laws from returning to the earthly plane unless a wrong is suffered.

attributions.surface_quote: No ego ever is permitted, by the very laws of its being, to go back to earth except a wrong thing is thereby suffered.

canonical_statement: A soul cannot return to the earthly plane without undergoing rebirth.

attributions.surface_quote: The soul can not return save it re-embody in rebirth.

canonical_statement: The period between death and rebirth is for the assimilation of past earthly experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: in devachan it assimilates the fruits of active earth-life.

canonical_statement: Reassociation of the ego with its astral shell after death is detrimental to the ego.

attributions.surface_quote: reassociation with the astral-shell... much to the detriment of the latter.

canonical_statement: During the post-mortem assimilation of past life, no new actions or thoughts can be generated.

attributions.surface_quote: I could do no new thing, think no new thought, experience nothing not in itself the expression of something done ere I came through the grave.

canonical_statement: Time does not function in the process of rearranging and crystallizing past earthly life experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: time cut no figure. The realness of it was; but the reality of vivid dreaming; time had no part in that which was already done.

canonical_statement: The astral body is a vivified force that perfectly reflects the image of its associated ego.

attributions.surface_quote: The astral is only vivified force, bearing the image in all respects of its ego, the I AM.

canonical_statement: Prophecies delivered by returned spirits may originate from the ego's foresight at the moment of its departure, imprinted upon its astral shell.

attributions.surface_quote: prophecies which come true after years, perhaps are but the impressed foresight of the ego at the moment of departure. And this glimpse in imprinted on its astral-shell.

canonical_statement: The duration for which an astral shell can sustain itself varies based on the decedent's spiritual orientation.

attributions.surface_quote: such sustenance in sufficient for ages, in others, centuries, years, days, or even minutes, according to the earthward-turning, or the spirit-turning sympathies of the decedent.

canonical_statement: Interfering with natural processes, such as recalling the departed, incurs a penalty proportional to the understanding of the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: no process of Nature as ordered by our Heavenly Father may be lightly interrupted; every such act carries penalty proportionate to the understanding of the culprit

canonical_statement: The astral body can continue to impress sensitives even after the ego has departed.

attributions.surface_quote: my "shell" might otherwise continue to impress. Thus might have resulted much trouble, for this astral of mine was but faithfully repeating my final words

canonical_statement: Psychic force is the fundamental controlling mechanism of existence, governing both celestial bodies and atomic structures.

attributions.surface_quote: It is psychic force which is their controlling lever, formed force. It is this same force which holds the stars to their orbits, and the atoms to theirs.

canonical_statement: Psychic force is dualistic, possessing both positive and negative aspects.

attributions.surface_quote: It is vital, and dual, being positive and negative.

canonical_statement: Specific focal points exist that absorb all lesser natural forces upon contact and represent the 'universal solvent'.

attributions.surface_quote: These focus points are portals whereinto the entire concourse of lesser forces of nature are absorbed upon contact. These foci are also the sole residence of the much sought 'universal solvent' of the alchemists

canonical_statement: These focal points are the 'auricles of the heart of the Universe' where all formed force reaches its culmination.

attributions.surface_quote: These foci are very auricles of the heart of the Universe, hence any sort of formed force meets here its Omega.

canonical_statement: The medulla oblongata functions as a 'maxin-point' in the body where positive and negative forces meet, essential for life.

attributions.surface_quote: On a very small scale indeed the medulla oblongata of the brain is such a focus, a maxin-point, where positive and negative meet. Were it not so, life would be impossible

canonical_statement: Individuals can voluntarily project their astral body to interact with others beyond the 'Divide', but those beyond cannot return to Earth.

attributions.surface_quote: how it is that those on earth can acquire the power of going to their friends beyond the Divide, but never these last come back to earth.

canonical_statement: A soul that has passed beyond the grave can be compelled to return to the earthly plane through the application of superior force.

attributions.surface_quote: a medium at a "spiritualistic seance" can bring back or down a soul which had gone on through the grave

canonical_statement: Forcing a soul to return from beyond the grave creates a disruptive psychic disturbance.

attributions.surface_quote: it will give rise to a psychic storm, and these are exceedingly costly occurrences.

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness perceives reality uniquely, shaping its own subjective world.

attributions.surface_quote: No two people see in the same way the same world.

canonical_statement: One's psychic plane, or subjective reality, is populated by the constructs of one's own mind, including experiences, hopes, and conceptions.

attributions.surface_quote: my psychic plane... was peopled with the children of my fancy, my experiences, my hopes, longings, aspirations, and my conceptions

canonical_statement: The post-mortem state, or heaven (devachan), is a realm where the soul assimilates the results of its previous life's actions and knowledge, rather than performing new actions.

attributions.surface_quote: the state after the grave... is the condition of harvest, where no one acts, but where the rewards of action... are paid

canonical_statement: The post-mortem state is devoid of earthly suffering such as pain, sorrow, sickness, or agony, as these conditions are exclusive to the earthly realm.

attributions.surface_quote: it is the land of Lethe, where is no pain, sorrow, sickness or agony, for these earthly conditions begun on earth, and they perforce must be finished on earth.

canonical_statement: The post-mortem state serves as a period of rest and assimilation for the soul, analogous to night's rest after day's activity, preparing for a new incarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: heaven... is to the former as the resting time of night is to the activity of the day.

canonical_statement: The nature of an individual's post-mortem experience (devachan) is determined by their actions and spiritual state during their earthly life, particularly regarding the overcoming of 'animal lusts'.

attributions.surface_quote: the devachan of one that hath committed earth-binding errors... is anything like the great Life wherewith are crowned those who are faithful unto the death of that serpent in the heart, animal lusts.

canonical_statement: The finite nature of human language and concepts is insufficient to describe the infinite, higher states of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Words can well portray mere devachan, they are powerless to depict that Life. Finite can never compass Infinite.

canonical_statement: Upon transitioning from the earthly life, an individual's perception of the physical world diminishes, replaced by new, tangible, and interactive sensory experiences of the afterlife.

attributions.surface_quote: my earthly powers were departing. The power which I had a moment before possessed of seeing persons, places and things of the world seemed fast escaping me, while glorious sights and sounds replaced them... these were real to my senses, tangible and mutually reactive.

canonical_statement: There is a separation between those in the earthly realm and those in the initial post-mortem state, preventing mutual perception.

attributions.surface_quote: if those left on Death's first shore could not see me nor know my presence, nor I see them nor their presence

canonical_statement: The experience of death does not necessarily entail the cessation of individual consciousness or identity.

attributions.surface_quote: the idea that I was dead. I no longer knew any such experience, and the knowledge of death had passed away

canonical_statement: Consciousness can persist and experience new realities after the physical body's demise.

attributions.surface_quote: the sight of the palace and of familiar things faded from view, and I seemed to have come into a beautiful valley

canonical_statement: Personal identity and memory can be fluid or subject to alteration across different states of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: I had forgotten as completely as if I had never known the life which I had experienced as Zailm

canonical_statement: Relationships and recognition can transcend the boundaries of physical life and memory.

attributions.surface_quote: Knowest thou me, thy father, Merin Numinos? ... I looked on him whom I recognized as my father.

canonical_statement: Memories of past lives or previous states of existence can be inaccessible, similar to forgotten dreams.

attributions.surface_quote: no memory of death, nothing. All had gone like the events of some dream which we strive in vain to recall

canonical_statement: New realities or experiences can resonate with pre-existing inner knowledge or archetypes, even if specific past memories are absent.

attributions.surface_quote: when I came across things in the new state similar to those known and loved in the old... I feel prefigured in my heart.

canonical_statement: The self can experience a state of being that aligns perfectly with its desires, independent of specific past memories.

attributions.surface_quote: I only knew that I experienced a state of things just suited to my desires.

canonical_statement: The afterlife involves a state where experiences are shaped by one's past life's aspirations and achievements.

attributions.surface_quote: not having reached such a degree on earth...I had no real basis from which to draw devachanic scenes.

canonical_statement: In the afterlife, conceptual constructs can manifest with the same perceived reality as physical entities or persons.

attributions.surface_quote: alone with my concepts, which...seemed as real as actual persons, for all seemed absolutely real.

canonical_statement: The afterlife allows for the manifestation of desired or imagined realities, which are perceived as natural.

attributions.surface_quote: It seemed perfectly natural to meet Anzimee one night as I wandered by the shore of a sea adjacent to an artificial wilderness...

canonical_statement: The afterlife is a state where the environment and one's perceived age can spontaneously alter in accordance with inner desires or past aspirations.

attributions.surface_quote: A change had come over. I was older; the landscape was different...correspondent with the later desires of my youth.

canonical_statement: The afterlife is a state where significant environmental and personal changes occur without being perceived as extraordinary by the experiencer.

attributions.surface_quote: These alterations...were not startling nor even remarkable to me.

canonical_statement: The described post-mortem state, while a 'life after death,' is distinct from a higher, ultimate spiritual existence with God.

attributions.surface_quote: it was the life after death...But this is not the Great Life with God.

canonical_statement: The physical universe and the spiritual realms are externalized ideas of a divine entity.

attributions.surface_quote: The earth and universe are the fiat, or externalized ideas of God.

canonical_statement: The phenomena of the physical and spiritual worlds are expressions or communications from a divine source.

attributions.surface_quote: The things of earth are words of God's great Word, speaking to us. So, too, are the things of devachan or heaven.

canonical_statement: Reality, both physical and spiritual, is subjectively experienced and exists within the perceiver.

attributions.surface_quote: Both are real, oppositely so, but only real within us, not without us.

canonical_statement: Mental habits and ingrained thought patterns persist beyond physical death.

attributions.surface_quote: In the process of death, habits of mind do not suffer extinction together with life's memories of events.

canonical_statement: The concept of linear time, as measured in 'years,' can apply to states of being beyond physical existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Even several years hast thou slept.

canonical_statement: Individuals in a post-mortem state may have no memory or knowledge of previous states of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: He evidently knew nothing, of any previous state, nor, by the very form of my question, did I know more than he.

canonical_statement: Death, as commonly understood, does not exist; it is merely a transition from an objective to a subjective state of being.

attributions.surface_quote: there is no such thing as death for a fact. Likewise pain and sorrow. ... there is no other death than the mere change from objective to subjective states of being

canonical_statement: Souls, upon entering the afterlife, perceive that the concept of death taught by earthly religions is a fiction.

attributions.surface_quote: many souls entering heaven conceive at the moment of death that no death exists, and that the teachings received on earth from priests were but ecclesiastical fictions.

canonical_statement: The experience of death is a change so profound that the disembodied soul does not recognize it as death.

attributions.surface_quote: death to the disembodied soul was and is an unknown conception.

canonical_statement: All souls experience a swift review of their past life immediately after the transition of death.

attributions.surface_quote: a swift view of the life just closed, a view all souls have, however brief it be.

canonical_statement: Earthly sorrows cease for the soul during its sojourn in devachan.

attributions.surface_quote: with death came the cessation of all earthly sorrow. This is true for a time limited by the length of the soul's sojourn in devachan.

canonical_statement: Earth-born influences are confined to the earthly plane and do not affect souls in devachan.

attributions.surface_quote: These earth-born mists do not intrude there for the reason that being earth born they must of necessity have abiding places on earth and influence only those on earth.

canonical_statement: Negative actions create a 'crystallized disposition' that persists and influences future incarnations.

attributions.surface_quote: The evil that men do lives after them... in the form of crystallized disposition to do wrong, lies in wait for their return to earth life

canonical_statement: The 'seed' of past wrongdoings, though dormant in devachan, manifests as sorrow in subsequent incarnations.

attributions.surface_quote: while the sinner is free of its power in devachan, the seed... is ready to grow a harvest of sorrow along with the growing life of the new incarnated one

canonical_statement: Evil actions continue to grow until atoned for by good actions.

attributions.surface_quote: until some good action shall atone for evil done, this evil will continue to grow.

canonical_statement: Humanity has an eternity to rectify past wrongs.

attributions.surface_quote: man hath an eternity in which to make repayment

canonical_statement: Following divine laws and acting righteously gradually eradicates the effects of past wrongs.

attributions.surface_quote: following God's laws and being true to right... the tares are little by little uprooted.

canonical_statement: A good act can erase a bad act.

attributions.surface_quote: A good act is the erasure of a bad

canonical_statement: Individual perception fundamentally shapes one's experienced reality, making each person's world unique.

attributions.surface_quote: the world is different to every person--not the same precisely in any two cases.

canonical_statement: The afterlife is a subjective reconstruction of earthly experiences, where concepts and perceptions from life become the new reality.

attributions.surface_quote: this after life is a reconstituted and inverted earth life, subjective now, instead of objective.

canonical_statement: Concepts held about others during life determine their manifestation in the afterlife.

attributions.surface_quote: if I die thinking him or her my friend, that concept is the one carried into the after life

canonical_statement: The 'self' exists as a concept within the subjective realities of others.

attributions.surface_quote: a concept of me existed in the imaged world of every friend I had.

canonical_statement: The soul records all experiences and thoughts on an imperishable mental substance, which forms the basis of post-mortem existence.

attributions.surface_quote: the record of the soul, made on imperishable mental substance, which constitutes much of the life after the grave

canonical_statement: Souls in Devachan can genuinely interact with other individual souls, especially when their earthly experiences were deeply intertwined.

attributions.surface_quote: Devachan would indeed be a drear heaven if the friends of mundane life were never aught but "dream faces."

canonical_statement: The experiences in Devachan, though seemingly real, are a process of assimilating and crystallizing the results of earthly interactions into character traits.

attributions.surface_quote: during the assimilation of its results, that is, during the crystallization of such results into traits of character

canonical_statement: The intensity of longing from an individual on Earth can enable their higher self or pure soul to project into another's plane of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Because she so longed from me that it developed and enabled her to project her pure soul into my plane.

canonical_statement: The soul cannot regress in its evolutionary journey.

attributions.surface_quote: she could come to me, but I could not go back to her. There is no retrogression.

canonical_statement: Experiences from a prior earthly life are assimilated and contribute to the development of the soul in an intermediate state.

attributions.surface_quote: in experiencing this reward, I also unconsciously assimilated the value of the previous life on earth.

canonical_statement: Subjective experiences in an intermediate state refine and enhance the soul's capacities and traits for future incarnations.

attributions.surface_quote: These schemes were now brought into the subjective state... From these apparent actions my capacities were developed...

canonical_statement: Reincarnation results in the manifestation of enhanced mental and spiritual faculties, which are products of prior life experiences and post-mortem development.

attributions.surface_quote: in a new incarnation I would come forth to mankind possessed of phrenological organs of increased power...

canonical_statement: Souls associated in one life are re-associated in subsequent incarnations due to shared developmental processes in the intermediate state.

attributions.surface_quote: reincarnation would reassociate us again on earth. And it has done so...

canonical_statement: Post-mortem experiences can lead to an intuitive understanding and inclination towards specific fields of knowledge in future lives.

attributions.surface_quote: from this came added ability as a geologist; in short, an intuitive knowledge of geology...

canonical_statement: Knowledge can be inherited from past lives rather than acquired in the current life.

attributions.surface_quote: Zerah Colburn... brought it, a legacy from the dead centuries, his past lives.

attributions.surface_quote: it is one of the earliest learned and easiest feats performed by the novitiate.

attributions.surface_quote: the processes of all life are carried on by what for our present purpose may be called magnetism

canonical_statement: The acquisition of profound spiritual knowledge is contingent upon the individual's capacity for self-governance and adherence to high moral principles.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Nine-tenths of the people of this world are unable to govern themselves well; they cannot in saneness expect to be made sharers of such awful knowledge as Siva represents.

canonical_statement: The actions and intentions of individuals and societies generate karmic consequences that influence future states of being and the collective reality.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Christianize the money power of this world, so that capital shall not work harm to men but good, and from good thus born the karma of the world will lead to the goodness of heart which gives calmness of soul

canonical_statement: The soul or consciousness persists through multiple incarnations, allowing for the eventual attainment of spiritual truths not realized in a single lifetime.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: though you who desire to study and know occult truths now may not see your hopes fruit in your present incarnation, yet in coming lives you will grasp these truths which elude you at present.

canonical_statement: The universe contains an immeasurable and boundless reservoir of wisdom and truth, accessible to those who seek it without dogmatic constraints.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: I saw before me a great ocean of wisdom, flashing in the light of truth, its horizon defined only by the voyager's temporary inability to go farther, its depth measurable only by that of the Universe. Free from the dogmatism of cramping creeds and of superstition, that ocean reaches out

canonical_statement: The Creator is veiled from the created, including humanity, as long as the soul focuses on creation rather than the Creator.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: mystery, that mystery which veils the Creator from the created, veils it from the joint Creator, man

canonical_statement: The veil between Creator and created will be lifted when temporal existence merges into eternity, and humanity transcends its current state.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Veils it until the aeons of time shall be swallowed up in eternity--beyond the stars...when man shall cease to be man

canonical_statement: Nirvana is not the cessation of being, but rather the gathering of 'Life the Less' into a totality, representing the sum of all parts.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Life the Less be gathered into Nirvana, sum of all the, parts. I repeat it, sum of all the parts, for it is not in any wise that horrible cessation of being

canonical_statement: The concept of 'God is nothing' signifies that God is not a singular entity but the totality of all things, the Eternal Father of Life.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: God is nothing" (that is, not one thing, but the sum of all things) should be construed as a denial of the being of God

canonical_statement: A being can manifest a physical form from smoke or other substances through a ceremonial act, embodying a genuine personality.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the cloud of smoke rapidly took the human form, into which the solid appearance of genuine personality was introduced

canonical_statement: The physical body is a temporary garment that can be consciously discarded or assumed by advanced beings.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the body is like unto a coat, to be put off or on at pleasure-by those who know how.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can achieve instantaneous transference to any location in the universe through desire alone, once freed from the physical body.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: when thou shalt be free of thy mundane body... thou hast but to desire such transference... and it is accomplished.

canonical_statement: There are multiple realms or 'mansions' of existence beyond the material universe, including a 'house of light' and a 'dwelling place of darkness'.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the illimitable realms of the Father hold many 'mansions' besides the universe of matter and the house of light, or the dwelling place of darkness.

canonical_statement: Advanced beings can transcend the limitations of the physical world, having mastered its secrets.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the physical nature had no secrets from him; but the illimitable realms of the Father hold many 'mansions'...

canonical_statement: Some advanced beings remain in the material universe not for personal gain, but to serve others.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: In this mansion of the material universe nothing remained for Mendocus to gain; he stayed but to give.

canonical_statement: The true Logos, or word of God, invoked by an individual, can release the soul from the physical body.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: only the word of God (the true Logos) by himself invoked could 'loose the silver cord.'

canonical_statement: Individuals who live in their spiritual nature possess direct knowledge of their unity with the divine source.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the man who lives in his spiritual nature does not believe, but knows that his being is one with God

canonical_statement: Intuition is the voice of the spirit, providing instantaneous and effortless perception of truth directly from the divine source, surpassing external methods of learning.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: His spirit speaks by the voice of intuition, informing him by a single flash of that which otherwise he would be long years in learning by external methods

canonical_statement: Earth is a component within a larger, multi-layered cosmic structure, which itself is only a small part of an infinitely vast divine creation.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Earth is a letter in a seven-fold alphabet; the stellar universe is but one book; its pages truly are myriad, its chapters legion, yet, besides this book, the library of the Creator is of endless number.

canonical_statement: Spiritual peace can be transmitted from one who fully possesses it to another who is close to its attainment.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Mendocus, Master, having it himself could give it, especially to one who, like Semla, was so near its attainment.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can exist independently of the physical body.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: It had not occurred to me that I was divested of my mortal casket, so easy had been my disembodiment.

canonical_statement: The experience of death, or disembodiment, can be easy and pleasant.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Death is, after the agony of illness for those long sick, as easy and pleasant an experience.

canonical_statement: The physical body is a temporary, gross form of life that can be cast aside.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: body death is but a casting aside of the grosser forms of life, which have served their purpose.

canonical_statement: True death occurs when consciousness does not return to the physical body.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: If thou wert not to re-enter thy corporeal body again, this would be death for thee.

canonical_statement: The 'I AM' aspect of consciousness does not return to earthly conditions until reincarnation, always on a higher plane of progress.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the I AM comes not into any earthly condition until it returns for reincarnation; and then always on a higher, never on a lower plane of progress

canonical_statement: A penalty for sin or incomplete severance from earthly desires prevents immediate and complete liberation after death.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: still exists a penalty of sin, or, what is the same thing, incomplete severance of one's self from desires for earthly experiences.

canonical_statement: After death, the soul enters a realm called 'devachan' (heaven/Summerland), not immediately its ultimate home.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: We go not immediately to mine own home, but into that realm where those go who have died from earth into devachan

canonical_statement: The 'I AM' cannot return from devachan to communicate with the living; only the astral soul or animal principle may do so, which is harmful.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: no ego returns out of devachan except it be forced, and this is harmful and vastly unjust to the ego. The astral soul and animal principle may thus return, but the I AM never.

canonical_statement: The 'I AM' has no consciousness of past earthly states or events.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: To the latter there is no past earth state; mind, I do not say for it, but to it. That is, it has no consciousness of anything earthly or of anything occurring on the earth.

canonical_statement: The living can perceive or access those in devachan, but those in devachan cannot perceive or access the living.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: We can go to them, but they can not come to us.

canonical_statement: Death itself is not agony and does not bring startling changes or bestow wonderful powers of foresight upon the soul.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: death is not in itself agony; that it brings no startling changes, and does not invest the soul born into the hereafter with any wonderful power of foresight.

canonical_statement: Death primarily grants freedom from the earthly body and a few concomitant powers, but nothing remarkable.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: there is but freedom given from the earthly body, and a few concomitant powers bestowed; nothing remarkable, considering that earth has no more hold on the soul.

canonical_statement: Souls who seek disenthralment from earth and have accumulated good karma are taken away from its prisoning conditions.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Such as these have worked for their brethren and accumulated a good and high karma which takes them away from the prisoning conditions of earth.

canonical_statement: A part of the self, responsible for earthly perceptions and memories, can be temporarily separated or suppressed to facilitate transition to another state of being.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: let us leave thy second self, that part of thee which perceives earthly things and preserves earthly memories.

canonical_statement: The physical form is transient and can be consciously discarded.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: I have no further use for this transient form... a man dissolving into smoke.

canonical_statement: Memory of the earthly world can be erased or suppressed during a transition to another state of existence.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: I no more remembered anything of the world... knowledge of the latter state is blotted out during sleep.

canonical_statement: There exists a subjective world where physical laws do not apply, distinct from the objective physical world.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: physical nature and laws do not reign here; they reign in the objective world, but not here, for this is the subjective world.

canonical_statement: The subjective world is non-physical, non-existent in a material sense, and imperceptible to material senses, yet it is real.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: in no sense physical or existent, nor perceptible to senses belonging to matter. Yet it is real.

canonical_statement: Both subjective and objective states originate from a singular divine Spirit.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: subjective states, no less than objective ones, are born of the Spirit of the Father.

canonical_statement: The subjective world is entirely non-material and is conceptually more distant from Earth than any physical star.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: farther from the earth than the farthest star... in no wise of material nature.

canonical_statement: The subjective and objective worlds perceive each other as unreal, with each viewing the other's reality as dream-like.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Things of earth to the inhabitants of this world are but dreams, and vice versa. To either, the other seems unreal.

canonical_statement: The subjective world is the true 'home' or origin point of the soul.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: This we are in is the 'Far away home of-the soul.'

canonical_statement: The principle of earthly sensing and memory is distinct from the true self and remains with the physical body after death.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: that principle of my terrene nature which was the seat of earthly sensing, and of memories of things perceived, was left with the body

canonical_statement: An astral shell, a remnant of the deceased's earthly nature, can be animated by a medium's vitality and interact with the living.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the astral shell of a man or woman who is dead. And the vitality of the medium may galvanize that shell

canonical_statement: The true ego, or 'I AM,' does not return to earthly circles or communicate from its higher plane.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: There is no return of the ego (the I AM) to circles, neither communion from their plane down

canonical_statement: The astral shell's prophetic abilities or knowledge of post-death events derive from the ego's brief, highly prophetic state at death or glimpses of its self-conceived afterlife.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: they are but records of the ego which for a few brief moments at death is sometimes highly prophetic, and sees forward

canonical_statement: Mediumship is a genuine phenomenon, but its common understanding of spirit communication is incorrect.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Mediumship is true; its ordinary explanation is false.

canonical_statement: During a mediumistic trance, the medium's vital force is transferred to a 'control' which is not the true spirit or ego.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: his or her vital force is transferred to the 'control' which is but a shell, and not the true spirit or ego.

canonical_statement: The 'control' in mediumship is a temporary, non-conscious shell animated by the medium's vital force, not a true spirit.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: the 'control' which is but a shell, and not the true spirit or ego.

canonical_statement: Mediums can access past events and make prophecies, acting like a reader of a record.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Like a reader of a book of record is that medium; events of the past are retold, and more or less accurate prophecies made

canonical_statement: The influence of historical figures on mediums is sustained by the continued impact of their works or beliefs on humanity.

attributions.chapter: TAKE THEREFORE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW
attributions.surface_quote: Just so long as the 'Commentaries' influence mankind, just that long will the 'spirit' of Caesar control mediums

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness can create and inhabit a subjective reality that is perceived as objectively real by the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: his world is merely a world of him own conception; it exists not for him who is his neighbor

canonical_statement: Beings can enter into the subjective reality and perception of another, thereby sharing their experience.

attributions.surface_quote: we will go to him, and enter into perception of those things which he sees

canonical_statement: The 'Mansion of the Father' is a universal domain where all individuals exist, regardless of their specific subjective realities.

attributions.surface_quote: Both persons will be existent in the Mansion of the Father

canonical_statement: Unrealized desires and intentions from a previous existence can manifest as perceived reality in a subsequent state of being.

attributions.surface_quote: he had hoped to see realized on earth. Yet he died without it, and coming to the world of effects, finds it all (to him only) a fact.

canonical_statement: Different individuals can exist on distinct 'psychic planes' within the same overarching reality.

attributions.surface_quote: his neighbor, who will be, as we shall see, on a different psychic plane

canonical_statement: The physical environment can be a direct manifestation of an individual's systematized knowledge and principles.

attributions.surface_quote: all seemed to be mechanical contrivances, and to exist for that great underlying principle of the designer, the systematization of his knowledge

canonical_statement: Disembodied souls can exist on the same plane of invention and realization as embodied minds.

attributions.surface_quote: many of them were real personifications, a few of whom were media like ourselves, but the majority "dead," that is, disembodied souls

canonical_statement: The experiences and characteristics developed in one life determine the conditions and traits of a subsequent reincarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: In his last life on earth he sowed the seeds of the one to come. Here, he enjoys the growth of those seeds.

canonical_statement: Negative traits or experiences in one life can be transmuted into positive qualities or serve a beneficial purpose in a future incarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: out of his future egotism will arise self-confidence.' His spirituality of temperament is large, his animal qualities well balanced and strong, and the good of all his conceit will manifest itself next as a governor of those forces which will lead men forward.

canonical_statement: All events and experiences ultimately serve a benevolent divine purpose.

attributions.surface_quote: all things under the hand of God work together for good!

canonical_statement: There are non-physical realms of existence, such as the devachanic realm, where disembodied consciousness can reside.

attributions.surface_quote: The Falls were in the devachanic realm of an author

canonical_statement: Imagination can manifest as reality in a non-physical domain.

attributions.surface_quote: figments of his imagination when penned, were here become what his desire had always painted, realities

canonical_statement: The soul persists beyond physical death and can reincarnate.

attributions.surface_quote: this author, who has been in his soul-home these many centuries, shall be one of its prophets, recarnified.

canonical_statement: Subjective realities are real to those who perceive them, but not necessarily to those on different planes of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: both states are real, but to those on the respective planes only.

canonical_statement: The afterlife is a period of assimilating the consequences of actions performed during earthly life.

attributions.surface_quote: life between the grave and the cradle...is a life of assimilation of results

canonical_statement: The afterlife shapes character by presenting the effects of past actions as causes for future earthly lives.

attributions.surface_quote: effects are so arranged as to present them as causes in the succeeding earth life

canonical_statement: The soul undergoes a process of rebirth on Earth after a period in Devachan.

attributions.surface_quote: the soul in devachan, which is perforce seeking rebirth on earth

canonical_statement: The universe operates under immutable laws of cause and effect, with no accidental or chance occurrences.

attributions.surface_quote: There is no accident, no chance, in the Universe; all is immutable law, cause and effect.

canonical_statement: Souls are attracted to specific parents for rebirth based on mental and spiritual similarities at the time.

attributions.surface_quote: children of that time are souls attracted from devachan to their mental similars

canonical_statement: Devachan is a realm where the environment is shaped by the concepts and experiences of its inhabitants.

attributions.surface_quote: we were in the concepts of an American who had resided for many years in Japan ere his entrance to devachan

canonical_statement: Reality can be subjectively constructed by an individual's consciousness, where perceived environments and beings are manifestations of their ideals and imagination.

attributions.surface_quote: all effects here, were arranged in accord with this man's ideals. In them he saw realized his dreams...

canonical_statement: Perception can be shared or 'insinuated' into another's subjective reality, allowing multiple observers to experience the same individually constructed environment.

attributions.surface_quote: because he saw them, we also saw them, for Mol Lang had insinuated our perceptions into this man's soul plane.

canonical_statement: Entities within a subjectively created reality conform to the creator's will and characteristics, even if they appear to be independent individuals.

attributions.surface_quote: the people whom he believed he saw... used no liquors more than he, for they were either his imagination's concepts, or... in sympathy with the master mind...

canonical_statement: An individual creating a subjective reality may be unaware that their experiences and the entities within them are their own creations, akin to a dreamer unaware of dreaming.

attributions.surface_quote: But all this he knew not any more than one who in slumber dreams, knows at the time that the vivid dream personages and places exist solely for himself.

canonical_statement: Genuine psychic journeys can occur between harmonious souls, distinct from mere subjective dreams, where the experience is a shared objective fact.

attributions.surface_quote: Sometimes, truly, a night dreamer really goes away with another harmonious soul, the two being real souls on a psychic journey, it being no dream, but a fact.

canonical_statement: Subjective creations, though imagined, can provide genuine joy and purpose to the creator.

attributions.surface_quote: all, things, was but quaffing imagined joys, wholly unconscious the while that they were subjective creations. They were all conceived for a single purpose, pursuit of which formed his chief joy...

canonical_statement: The experience of time is subjective and relative to the experiencer's perception and activity, rather than an objective, fixed duration.

attributions.surface_quote: Time is, after all, only a measure of so much done by or to him who experiences its lapse

canonical_statement: The duration of subjective time can diverge significantly from objective or commonly accepted temporal measurements.

attributions.surface_quote: myriads of people have lived a whole century during ten minutes

canonical_statement: Shared experiences can lead to a profound sense of unity and identity between individuals, suggesting a commonality of being.

attributions.surface_quote: We were two souls on the same plane, reaping identical experiences.

canonical_statement: Music can facilitate a transcendent state where individual identity dissolves into a universal, harmonious consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: my being had become a personless, throbbing, sobbing stress of harmony

canonical_statement: The astral body can be separated from the conscious self and left in a physical location.

attributions.surface_quote: my own astral had been left behind in the Sakaza on earth

canonical_statement: Perception of reality is limited by the available means of comparison or reference points.

attributions.surface_quote: I had no means of comparison of ideas. The place I was in was the only place existent for me

canonical_statement: Memory shells are formed by the self as it experiences different places or concepts.

attributions.surface_quote: a memory shell had been formed by me as I went through them

canonical_statement: Individuals in the afterlife may perceive an idealized version of a loved one rather than their true form.

attributions.surface_quote: the American really had not his daughter with him, but only his ideal of her

canonical_statement: Transitions in the psychic realm can occur without conscious awareness of the mechanism or timing.

attributions.surface_quote: without my knowing just how or when, we had left the boat and the lake, and were in a garden

canonical_statement: Astonishment is not a typical reaction to events in the psychic realm.

attributions.surface_quote: No one is ever astonished at anything in the psychic realm.

canonical_statement: The devachanic concepts of the soul differ from the actual objects or individuals conceived.

attributions.surface_quote: what difference exists between the devachanic concepts of the soul and the objects conceived of

canonical_statement: The nature of 'heaven' is determined by individual creation or perception.

attributions.surface_quote: It illustrates the saying that 'heaven is what we make it.'

canonical_statement: Beings in the psychic realm may be imperceptible to those in a different state of existence or awareness.

attributions.surface_quote: She seemed not to perceive us

canonical_statement: The perception of physical reality is contingent upon one's psychic condition.

attributions.surface_quote: if we were in a different psychic condition, the earth would not be near, but vastly remote from us.

canonical_statement: Significant societal reforms and great good cannot fully succeed in periods designated by the number nine.

attributions.surface_quote: no great reform, nor anything greatly good, can succeed in any century, decade or year nominated by the number nine.

canonical_statement: The afterlife, or 'devachan,' is constructed from unfulfilled hopes, longings, and aspirations from earthly life.

attributions.surface_quote: our devachan, our heaven, is made; but from those hopes, longings, aspirations and determinations which through life are our dearest desires because we have never been able to satisfy them.

canonical_statement: On Earth, individuals do not perceive others directly, but rather interact with their own self-created conceptual images of them.

attributions.surface_quote: even on earth we do not have our friends, but only our concepts of them

canonical_statement: True spiritual connection and togetherness, both in life and the afterlife, is achieved through the identity or alignment of thoughts and ideals between souls.

attributions.surface_quote: only identity of thought makes nearness of souls.

canonical_statement: The ultimate spiritual evolution involves all souls converging into a state of complete unity with each other and with the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: none shall be apart from any other, or from the Father.

canonical_statement: The afterlife realm known as Devachan is a place of rest for occult students and adepts after physical death.

attributions.surface_quote: The Lunar Temple, a part of devachan... Here, where many occult students come after laying aside the earthly body, is a holy place of rest.

canonical_statement: The experience of Devachan varies based on an individual's spiritual development and understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: devachan to them is not, therefore, on the same plane as with other mortals, any more than their objective life was.

canonical_statement: Souls can reincarnate after a period of rest in the afterlife, with future incarnations influenced by past life experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: He will then incarnate... because his life has been mostly spent in that land this time.

canonical_statement: True matter is a singular, fundamental substance beyond human sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Matter is a One Substantiality, having not a single quality which any human sense can cognize.

canonical_statement: The spiritual vision allows for the perception of non-physical realities.

attributions.surface_quote: they saw then with eyes of spirit, hence had then, as now, much the same concepts of life

canonical_statement: Force is a creation of the divine and possesses two polarities: positive and negative.

attributions.surface_quote: force also is one of the creations of the Father. And force hath two polarities, the positive and the negative

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses seven senses, with five currently evolved and two remaining undeveloped.

attributions.surface_quote: man on earth hath certain senses; seven are these senses: sight, hearing, feeling, smelling, tasting, intuition, and one innominate.

canonical_statement: The physical world is a 'Mansion of Cause' associated with positive force, while the afterlife (devachan) is a 'Mansion of effects' associated with negative force.

attributions.surface_quote: earth (cause) and devachan (effect) are material; both due in their every phenomena to force

canonical_statement: Both the physical world and the afterlife are material, but each is only cognizable by senses specific to that state.

attributions.surface_quote: both earth (cause) and devachan (effect) are material; both due in their every phenomena to force, but either state is cognizable only by senses special to it.

canonical_statement: Both the physical world and the afterlife are ultimately unreal except from the perspective of the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: Yet both states are really material, and similarly, both are unreal except to the Father.

canonical_statement: Human existence involves a cyclical process of dying from one state and being born into another, alternating between physical incarnation and discarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: Man is constantly dying from the one state and being born in the other, back and forth, and only that state where he is is real to him at any time.

canonical_statement: Each cycle of rebirth on Earth leads to a higher plane of existence, culminating in the attainment of a 'conditionless' state (Nirvana) where humanity reunites with the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: each time of rebirth on the earth finds him ever on a higher plane, until at last the concrete condition miscalled life is over, and the conditionless 'long devachan' (Nirvana) is attained. Then man and his Father are together and at-one.

canonical_statement: Humanity originated from the divine and is destined to return to it.

attributions.surface_quote: Man came from God; unto Him must he go.

canonical_statement: Memories of certain experiences can be intentionally suppressed or erased from an individual's conscious recollection.

attributions.surface_quote: Mol Lang had no desire that I should continuously retain the memories... separate facts were to become quite as unknown.

canonical_statement: Experiences, even if consciously forgotten, can still exert an influence on the soul's spiritual progression.

attributions.surface_quote: All was solely for the purpose of surrounding my soul with influences calculated to force me upward and onward.

canonical_statement: The ultimate purpose of certain life experiences is to guide the soul towards a higher spiritual state, away from earthly desires.

attributions.surface_quote: force me upward and onward, out of earth life, or desire for it, until at last I would come to realize that I had known something higher.

canonical_statement: The perception of life's significance varies greatly between ordinary human understanding and occult or spiritually advanced perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Grand as the vision of life seemeth to the ordinary man... to me it is infinitely more sublime.

canonical_statement: Conventional human understanding of life, including concepts of earthly existence and heaven, is often flawed and incomplete.

attributions.surface_quote: Man's ideas are full of error; they involve the childishness of admitting that in the life on earth...

canonical_statement: Only through a 'Great Master' can an individual initiate infinite causes with eternal psychic effects within a finite earthly lifespan.

attributions.surface_quote: Only through the Great Master are any so able.

canonical_statement: Memories can be erased by disassociating the astral body formed by experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: It is easy to erase these memories; I have but to disassociate the astral body here formed by thine experiences.

canonical_statement: Forgotten states or experiences can be accessed again when the astral body controls an individual as its medium.

attributions.surface_quote: thou wilt thereafter know this state only when that astral shall control thee as its medium.

canonical_statement: An individual's karma dictates future earthly incarnations and periods of atonement.
